title: Built an AI-powered stock news intelligence bot — looking for honest feedback
author: INDIAN_JARVIS
selftext:
I've been working on a SaaS-style project that helps investors consume market news faster.

Instead of displaying raw headlines, the system analyzes each news event and generates:

Sentiment analysis

Impact score

Investment horizon

Key opportunities

Key risks

Stocks potentially affected

The goal is to reduce information overload and help users identify which news items deserve deeper research.

One challenge has been balancing speed with accuracy. News can be published in seconds, but generating useful context without hallucinations is much harder than simply summarizing text.

Current stack:

Python

FastAPI

LLM-based analysis pipeline

Telegram delivery

I'm curious:

Would you pay for a tool like this?

What would make it more valuable than existing news platforms?

What metrics would you want to see before trusting AI-generated market analysis?

Looking for brutally honest feedback before I continue building.

comments.author: datedbrent
comments.body: id want to connect to my own models as one input and test. how much id pay depends on the additional edge this may provide

replies.author: INDIAN_JARVIS
replies.body:
That's fair.
My goal isn't to compete with custom models or replace existing workflows. The focus is on reducing information overload and providing a consistent first-pass analysis layer.
For me, the real challenge is proving whether the impact scoring and prioritization add measurable value beyond raw news feeds and generic LLM summaries.
I'm currently exploring ways to benchmark outputs against historical market reactions and measure consistency across similar news events.
If you're already running your own models, what kind of edge or metrics would convince you that an external analysis layer is worth integrating?
